lines.text: Pick four corners of this thirteen-sided shape, and join them up.
lines.caption: Pick four corners of this thirteen-sided shape, and join them up.

lines.text: Sometimes the shape covers the center dot, and sometimes it misses. <short pause> Which happens more?
lines.caption: Sometimes the shape covers the center dot, and sometimes it misses. Which happens more?

lines.text: Hi there, I'm Vantee! Today's trick is to count the misses instead of the hits.
lines.caption: Hi there, I'm Vantee! Today's trick is to count the misses instead of the hits.

lines.text: Here's the question. Four of the thirteen vertices of a regular thirteen-sided polygon are chosen.
lines.caption: Here's the question. Four of the thirteen vertices of a regular thirteen-sided polygon are chosen.

lines.text: They are joined in order to make a quadrilateral.
lines.caption: They are joined in order to make a quadrilateral.

lines.text: For how many choices of the four vertices does the quadrilateral contain the center?
lines.caption: For how many choices of the four vertices does the quadrilateral contain the center?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: Let's break it down. A vertex is a corner. These thirteen vertices sit evenly around a circle.
lines.caption: Let's break it down. A vertex is a corner. These thirteen vertices sit evenly around a circle.

lines.text: Join four of them in order around the circle, and you get a quadrilateral.
lines.caption: Join four of them in order around the circle, and you get a quadrilateral.

lines.text: This one holds the center inside. That's a hit.
lines.caption: This one holds the center inside. That's a hit.

lines.text: This one misses the center completely.
lines.caption: This one misses the center completely.

lines.text: No vertex sits directly across from another, so the center is never right on a side.
lines.caption: No vertex sits directly across from another, so the center is never right on a side.

lines.text: How many choices in all? Thirteen ways to pick a first vertex, then twelve, eleven, and ten.
lines.caption: How many choices in all? Thirteen ways to pick a first vertex, then twelve, eleven, and ten.

lines.text: But each group of four shows up in twenty-four orders: four times three times two times one.
lines.caption: But each group of four shows up in twenty-four orders: four times three times two times one.

lines.text: Divide by twenty-four, and you get seven hundred fifteen choices in all.
lines.caption: Divide by twenty-four, and you get seven hundred fifteen choices in all.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Counting the hits directly is tricky. So let's count the misses, and subtract.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Counting the hits directly is tricky. So let's count the misses, and subtract.

lines.text: Look at one side of the quadrilateral. It cuts off an arc with no chosen vertices on it.
lines.caption: Look at one side of the quadrilateral. It cuts off an arc with no chosen vertices on it.

lines.text: If that empty arc is less than half the circle, the center stays on the inside of that side.
lines.caption: If that empty arc is less than half the circle, the center stays on the inside of that side.

lines.text: If one empty arc is MORE than half the circle, that side cuts the center off. The shape misses it.
lines.caption: If one empty arc is MORE than half the circle, that side cuts the center off. The shape misses it.

lines.text: So a choice misses exactly when all four vertices squeeze into half of the circle.
lines.caption: So a choice misses exactly when all four vertices squeeze into half of the circle.

lines.text: How many vertices fit in a half? Going all the way around takes thirteen steps.
lines.caption: How many vertices fit in a half? Going all the way around takes thirteen steps.

lines.text: Half of that is six and a half steps.
lines.caption: Half of that is six and a half steps.

lines.text: So a half holds a first vertex and the next six vertices. The seventh one is past halfway.
lines.caption: So a half holds a first vertex and the next six vertices. The seventh one is past halfway.

lines.text: Let's count the misses. Go clockwise. The first vertex comes right after the big empty arc.
lines.caption: Let's count the misses. Go clockwise. The first vertex comes right after the big empty arc.

lines.text: The other three vertices must be among the next six.
lines.caption: The other three vertices must be among the next six.

lines.text: Six choose three is six times five times four, over six for the orders. That's twenty ways.
lines.caption: Six choose three is six times five times four, over six for the orders. That's twenty ways.

lines.text: The first vertex can be any of the thirteen vertices.
lines.caption: The first vertex can be any of the thirteen vertices.

lines.text: So thirteen times twenty gives two hundred sixty misses.
lines.caption: So thirteen times twenty gives two hundred sixty misses.

lines.text: Could one miss get counted twice? No! It has only one empty arc bigger than half.
lines.caption: Could one miss get counted twice? No! It has only one empty arc bigger than half.

lines.text: A bigger-than-half arc is at least seven steps. Two need fourteen steps, but there are only thirteen.
lines.caption: A bigger-than-half arc is at least seven steps. Two need fourteen steps, but there are only thirteen.

lines.text: So the hits are seven hundred fifteen minus two hundred sixty: four hundred fifty-five. Choice C!
lines.caption: So the hits are seven hundred fifteen minus two hundred sixty: four hundred fifty-five. Choice C!

lines.text: Here's another way. The four gaps between chosen vertices always add up to thirteen steps.
lines.caption: Here's another way. The four gaps between chosen vertices always add up to thirteen steps.

lines.text: A miss has one big gap of seven steps or more. The other three gaps share what's left.
lines.caption: A miss has one big gap of seven steps or more. The other three gaps share what's left.

lines.text: If the big gap is seven steps, the other three gaps add up to six. Let's list them: ten ways.
lines.caption: If the big gap is seven steps, the other three gaps add up to six. Let's list them: ten ways.

lines.text: A big gap of eight steps leaves five. That's six ways.
lines.caption: A big gap of eight steps leaves five. That's six ways.

lines.text: A gap of nine leaves four: three ways. A gap of ten leaves three: just one way.
lines.caption: A gap of nine leaves four: three ways. A gap of ten leaves three: just one way.

lines.text: Ten plus six plus three plus one is twenty. That's the same twenty as before!
lines.caption: Ten plus six plus three plus one is twenty. That's the same twenty as before!

lines.text: The big gap can start at any of the thirteen vertices, so again there are two hundred sixty misses.
lines.caption: The big gap can start at any of the thirteen vertices, so again there are two hundred sixty misses.

lines.text: When would you pick each? The first vertex is fastest. The gaps show WHY there's one big gap.
lines.caption: When would you pick each? The first vertex is fastest. The gaps show WHY there's one big gap.

lines.text: Choice E, seven hundred fifteen, counts every choice. It forgets about the center.
lines.caption: Choice E, seven hundred fifteen, counts every choice. It forgets about the center.

lines.text: Choice A, two hundred sixty, is the number of misses. Don't forget to subtract!
lines.caption: Choice A, two hundred sixty, is the number of misses. Don't forget to subtract!

lines.text: Choice D, five hundred twenty, picks all four vertices from the next six. That's only fifteen ways.
lines.caption: Choice D, five hundred twenty, picks all four vertices from the next six. That's only fifteen ways.

lines.text: That gives one hundred ninety-five misses, and five hundred twenty hits.
lines.caption: That gives one hundred ninety-five misses, and five hundred twenty hits.

lines.text: But the first vertex is already one of the four, so only three more come from the next six.
lines.caption: But the first vertex is already one of the four, so only three more come from the next six.

lines.text: Choice B, three hundred ninety, needs twenty-five misses per first vertex. We found only twenty.
lines.caption: Choice B, three hundred ninety, needs twenty-five misses per first vertex. We found only twenty.

lines.text: So here's a great habit: when the hits are hard to count, count the misses and subtract.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit: when the hits are hard to count, count the misses and subtract.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? This time, take a regular eleven-sided polygon.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? This time, take a regular eleven-sided polygon.

lines.text: Choose three of its vertices to make a triangle. How many of these triangles contain the center?
lines.caption: Choose three of its vertices to make a triangle. How many of these triangles contain the center?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Eleven times ten times nine, over six for the orders, is one hundred sixty-five triangles.
lines.caption: Eleven times ten times nine, over six for the orders, is one hundred sixty-five triangles.

lines.text: Five steps is less than half of eleven, and six is more. So a half holds the first vertex and the next five.
lines.caption: Five steps is less than half of eleven, and six is more. So a half holds the first vertex and the next five.

lines.text: The other two vertices come from those five. Five choose two is ten ways.
lines.caption: The other two vertices come from those five. Five choose two is ten ways.

lines.text: Eleven first vertices times ten ways gives one hundred ten misses.
lines.caption: Eleven first vertices times ten ways gives one hundred ten misses.

lines.text: One hundred sixty-five minus one hundred ten is fifty-five triangles.
lines.caption: One hundred sixty-five minus one hundred ten is fifty-five triangles.

lines.text: If you found fifty-five, amazing work!
lines.caption: If you found fifty-five, amazing work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea: when the hits are hard to count, count the misses, and subtract.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea: when the hits are hard to count, count the misses, and subtract.

lines.text: Here, a miss has all its vertices in one half, so count each miss by its first vertex.
lines.caption: Here, a miss has all its vertices in one half, so count each miss by its first vertex.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
